task.instruction: Find a report on the BBC News website about recent developments in renewable energy technologies in the UK.

final_answer:
I found a suitable BBC News report: **"Geothermal plant plans to drill four more wells"** (BBC News, Cornwall — published about 4 days ago, by Lee Trewhela of the Local Democracy Reporting Service).

**What it reports:** Eden Geothermal, operator of the UK's first geothermal power plant at the Eden Project in Cornwall, has applied to expand its underground drilling from the two wells previously permitted to six — four additional wells — in order to increase on-site renewable generation capacity without extending beyond the already approved site boundary. The current well reaches roughly 4.8–5 km below the surface and taps water at up to 200°C, which heats Eden's greenhouses and rainforest biome. Other proposed changes include a larger air-cooled condenser bank, reconfigured site buildings, two substations instead of one, and a smaller water storage lagoon. Cornwall Council's landscape team supported the mitigation measures, though they noted construction could cause dust and noise disturbance. Nearby residents can discuss the plans at Trethurgy Village Hall on Wednesday 15:00–19:00 GMT and on 6 November 15:00–18:00, with a determination date of 18 November.

**Why it fits:** it's a current BBC News item on a UK renewable-energy technology development (geothermal power in Cornwall). If you'd prefer a broader technology-focused piece, BBC Future also has a recent report, *"'It's offensively cheap': How solar power is quietly becoming bigger than nuclear"* (bbc.com/future/article/20261023-how-solar-became-bigger-than-nuclear), which covers the global solar surge including UK and Ember think-tank data.

judge.rationale: The final page is a BBC News article about the UK's first geothermal plant expanding wells to increase renewable energy generation, matching the request.

final_page.title: Eden Geothermal plans to drill four more wells in Cornwall
